request.spec:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has grace days (settings, a whole number, blank means off, not dated; SETTING_CHANGED
key=grace-days value=<days>). When the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date
plus the grace days is before the new today is closed, in order of their to-dates, exactly as a
close by hand would, each writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end; these lines come after
the new today is set and before the rollup lines of the today change.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now has a grace-days setting, and changing today closes every open period that is past its grace days. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**Setting**
- New migration `V38__grace_days.sql` adds a `grace_days` column to the sheet. Like period-numbering-from, it is not dated, and blank (null) means off.
- The setting goes through the existing settings steps: the request is checked as a whole number of days or blank, saved, and returned in the response. Saving it writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=grace-days value=<days>`.
- The settings form has a new `setting-grace-days` input and a `setting-grace-days-current` display.

**Auto close**
- `AutoClosePeriods` is a new step in `today.POST.yml`, placed between `SaveToday` and `AuditRollup`. That puts its lines after the new today is set and before the rollup lines.
- It closes each open period whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today, in to-date order. Each close writes `PERIOD_CLOSED … total=<x> auto=yes` when it happens.
- To close "exactly as a close by hand would", I moved the total-fixing logic out of `ClosePeriod` into a static `fix` method that both paths use. It is package-private, because OfficeFloor won't start if a step class has more than one public method.

**Decision for you:** auto close skips the "close" permission check. Changing today closes overdue periods even when the user's role isn't allowed to close by hand. The tests don't cover this. If auto close should follow the permission matrix, the choice is whether to skip those periods or refuse the today change.
